source_title: Now Available on Qdrant Cloud: GPU Indexing, Multi-AZ, and Audit Logging
claim_summary: Qdrant states GPU-accelerated HNSW indexing (up to 4x faster builds per its own benchmarks; NVIDIA T4; AWS only), Multi-AZ replication on the Premium tier (99.95% uptime SLA) and audit logging with user/API-key attribution on all paid clusters are available now
feature: managed-cloud GPU indexing; multi-AZ; audit logs
availability: GPU indexing AWS only; Multi-AZ Premium tier only and cannot be changed after cluster creation; audit logging paid clusters only
limitation: Vendor announcement; 4x figure is a vendor benchmark not independently reproduced; managed service is proprietary (engine is Apache-2.0)

claim_summary: Adds TurboQuant quantization, an API to add/delete named vectors in an existing collection, memory breakdown reporting, low-memory mode, strict-mode memory guardrail; fully removes RocksDB support; adds enforcement of API key/JWT auth on internal gRPC endpoints and an option to disable snapshot restore from URL; startup message links to agentic skills
feature: vector compression; schema evolution without reindex; internal-API auth
availability: GitHub release published 2026-05-11T15:04Z; Apache-2.0 repository; qdrant-client 1.18.0 on PyPI the same day
limitation: Release notes are vendor-authored; RocksDB removal is a storage migration concern for self-hosters; the new internal-auth option was later found to accept read-only credentials (see advisory row)

claim_summary: Vendor reports 4-bit TurboQuant recall close to scalar quantization at twice the compression on four datasets (HNSW m=16, ef_construct=128) and describes a query-audit-log API, request tracing IDs, per-collection API metrics and new strict-mode guardrails
feature: quantization; audit-log query API; tracing IDs
limitation: Recall tables are vendor-run on vendor-chosen datasets; blog itself says TurboQuant may slightly underperform scalar quantization on some data; no independent replication located

claim_summary: Patch release with consensus, filter and resharding fixes and a security fix to authorize a request before accepting a snapshot file upload
limitation: No GitHub security advisory or CVE was published for the snapshot-upload authorization fix (repository advisory list shows only two advisories); severity unknown

claim_summary: PyPI records qdrant-edge-py 0.7.0 first uploaded 2026-05-27T10:07Z (then 0.7.1 May 28, 0.7.2 Jun 1, 0.8.0 Aug 5) with license expression Apache-2.0
availability: beta per vendor; Apache-2.0 per PyPI metadata
limitation: Registry metadata shows publication only, not functionality or downstream use; release notes for Edge versions were not located; 0.6.x was pre-window

claim_summary: Private Cloud operator release adds support for Qdrant 1.18 and configuring audit logging through spec.config.audit on QdrantCluster
feature: self-hosted Kubernetes operator; audit logging config
limitation: Changelog page is undated as a whole (datePublished placeholder); per-version dates are as stated in headings; operator source licence not checked

claim_summary: Patch release fixing a REST auth whitelist bypass on specially crafted paths (route resolved before authorizing) and an out-of-bounds heap read with a malicious snapshot, plus optimizer and transfer fixes
feature: auth bypass and snapshot parsing fixes
limitation: Security fixes disclosed only as release-note lines; no advisory/CVE located in GitHub repository advisories or NVD keyword search; affected versions and exploitability not stated

source_title: Memory at the Edge: On-Device Vector Search with Qdrant Edge
claim_summary: Qdrant describes Edge as the Qdrant engine embedded in-process (~11 MB footprint, no server), free to use and in beta, and reports an in-house test of ~0.1 ms on-device vs ~52 ms round trip to Qdrant Cloud over cellular
availability: beta; pip install qdrant-edge-py / cargo add qdrant-edge
limitation: Blog states figures are in-house measurements, not an official benchmark; robot demo repo qdrant-labs/edge-mission-control shows no detected licence via GitHub API (2026-10-16)

source_title: Elasticsearch vs. Qdrant: 7x faster vector search
claim_summary: Elastic reports its DiskBBQ index reaching up to 7x higher throughput than Qdrant at comparable recall on network-attached storage and attributes Qdrant's latency to random disk reads during rescoring
limitation: Competitor-run benchmark of a rival; Qdrant (2026-07-08) disputed the configuration and Elastic's own follow-up (2026-07-13) says the disk-read mechanism it named does not survive its later arithmetic

source_title: Qdrant Lands in SF: Vector Space Day 2026 Recap
claim_summary: Qdrant reports over 350 attendees at its 2026-06-11 San Francisco event with Agents and Memory, Search and Retrieval, and Edge and Robotics tracks; CEO keynote names Rust core, GridStore, GPU indexing and TurboQuant
limitation: Attendance is vendor-reported; event attention is not adoption or reuse; talk content summarized by the vendor

source_title: Branch-Aware Semantic Code Search with Qdrant
claim_summary: Qdrant publishes a branch-aware semantic code-search pattern (one point per named declaration, payload filter over branch ancestry) so coding agents retrieve the version a branch actually runs; demo indexed 141 functions from Qdrant's own source
feature: version-scoped code retrieval for coding agents
availability: tutorial pattern; not a product feature
limitation: Single illustrative query on a small corpus; no retrieval-quality evaluation or accepted-task outcome; rebases/merges explicitly scoped out

source_title: Qdrant Beats Elastic's DiskBBQ at 2x Throughput, Half the Latency, and 1/3 the Compute
claim_summary: Qdrant reports on the same wiki_dpr_e5 dataset (21M x 768d) with TurboQuant 4-bit, originals on disk, async scorer and two-stage retrieval: 67.2 QPS / 59.5 ms on 3 x 2 vCPU/8 GB vs Elastic's published 32.4 QPS / 122.6 ms (2.1x throughput at matched recall); reproduction kit published
limitation: Vendor benchmark changing several variables at once (hardware, quantization, async scorer, replication); reproduction repo qdrant-labs/wiki-dpr-disk-rescore-benchmark shows no detected licence; disputed by Elastic 2026-07-13

source_title: The disk that never woke up: what actually decided our Qdrant vector search benchmark rematch
claim_summary: Elastic reproduced Qdrant's setup and reports both engines in the same range (about 56 QPS id-isolated vs Qdrant's 53-67) at ~0.96 recall; disk held at 0 IOPS during the run; Docker's default seccomp blocked io_uring (Operation not permitted) so the async scorer silently fell back; segment count drove most of the gap
limitation: Competitor-authored, adversarial rather than neutral; not independently re-run here; Elastic concedes its original 7x mechanism was not supported; the io_uring/seccomp observation is a reproducibility hazard for self-hosters

claim_summary: Private Cloud operator 2.34.0 tightens operator RBAC to least privilege (namespace-scoped Roles, limited Lease access, create-only VolumeAttributesClass), feature-gates Traefik write permissions and removes unused ServiceAccount/Role/SCC permissions
limitation: Vendor changelog only; RBAC scope not independently audited

claim_summary: Python client removes the fastembed-backed add and query convenience methods and deprecates search, search_batch, search_groups, recommend, recommend_batch, recommend_groups and on_disk_payload in favour of query_points and the new payload config; multiple local-mode fixes
limitation: Removal of add/query breaks downstream code and tutorials that used them; migration cost not measured

claim_summary: Adds TurboQuant 4-bit as a primary storage datatype (Turbo4, no full-precision copy), unified memory tiers (cold/cached/pinned), per-tenant IDF for sparse/BM25 search, keyword prefix match, slice filter, global quota API and read-routing token; removes deprecated search endpoints from OpenAPI; fixes a path traversal in S3-based snapshots
feature: hybrid/BM25 multi-tenant scoring; storage compression; memory tiers
availability: GitHub release published 2026-08-05T11:26Z; blog the same day
limitation: Vendor release notes; release blog states ninefold storage reduction trades away rescoring against originals (lower max recall); S3 path traversal fix has no published advisory

claim_summary: Qdrant's website source adds a Serverless landing page; the live page (read 2026-10-16) says 'COMING SOON', invites a waitlist and says access will roll out in stages starting with a limited group
limitation: Commit date dates the page, not a product launch; live page is mutable and undated; the 2025 public roadmap said Qdrant did not plan a separate serverless product, which this page may or may not contradict (unresolved)

source_title: Qdrant and Minima Deliver 2.92x More Agentic RAG Tasks per GPU-Hour
claim_summary: Partner-run test across 1,800 tasks reports hybrid (dense+BM25, RRF, late-interaction rerank) retrieval plus Minima inference raising successful throughput from 1,081 to 3,158 tasks per GPU-hour and grounded success from 80.1% to 84.2%; first-pass evidence sufficiency 72% to 87%
feature: hybrid retrieval in a bounded agent loop
limitation: Partner/vendor co-marketing; Minima's acceptance criteria self-set; 'grounded task success' grader and task sets not independently reviewed; GPU-hours are not energy

source_title: Enough with the Bad Benchmarks: Tools for Production-Grade Research
claim_summary: Qdrant releases Qdrant-FineWeb-10B (about 10B dense and 10B sparse gte-multilingual-base vectors; exact top-1000 ground truth), PubMed-Multi-Vector and Coyo-Vector-Embeddings, and open-sources the Supernova benchmarking framework
feature: open retrieval benchmark data and tooling
availability: datasets on Hugging Face (FineWeb-10B tagged ODC-BY); qdrant-labs/supernova Apache-2.0
limitation: Page gives 120,000 queries in one sentence and 100,000 in another and both '~25 TiB' and '24.47 TB' (internal inconsistency); usefulness for neutral benchmarking not yet independently demonstrated

source_title: Qdrant Builds a 10-Billion-Document Vector Search Benchmark Dataset on Vultr
claim_summary: Vultr states it provided compute and object storage, the 10-billion-document corpus was processed in about five days into about 25 TB from 500,000 files, and the dataset has 120,000 queries with exact ground truth
limitation: Infrastructure partner, not independent; does not quantify energy; a Business Wire syndication on 01net returned HTTP 403 and was not read

claim_summary: Patch release with batched HNSW and quantized-scoring performance work, crash-safety for transfers, rejection of vector size >65536 and empty dense vectors, a fix where omitting scroll limit bypassed max_query_limit, and a security fix rejecting '.' and '..' in collection names
limitation: Security fix not accompanied by a published advisory; performance claims not measured

claim_summary: Qdrant reports rewriting cross-encoder inference in Rust (cross-encode-rs) gave only ~1.1x median speedup over fastembed and sentence-transformers on a small model and ~1.4x on a larger one, because all three use onnxruntime; the largest gap came from configuration, not language
availability: library on a personal GitHub account
limitation: Vendor-authored micro-benchmark; repo AstraBert/cross-encode-rs shows no detected licence via GitHub API, so reuse rights are unclear; a near-null result for a rewrite is informative for reuse-first decisions

source_title: Constella Preview: Swap Query Models Without Re-Embedding
claim_summary: Qdrant publishes Constella Zero and Nano (34.5M-parameter) query encoders distilled to Stella's embedding space so a collection embedded with Stella can be queried with cheaper models without re-embedding; reports nDCG@10 on 15 BEIR datasets
availability: research preview; models on Hugging Face (constella-nano tagged MIT)
limitation: Vendor evaluation; distillation harness on a personal GitHub account with no detected licence; BEIR results not independently reproduced

claim_summary: Patch release accepting only read-write API keys on the internal gRPC API, allowing internal gRPC on a separate interface, adding a startup warning when no API keys are configured, adding GCS and Azure Blob snapshot storage, and fixing zero results when the HNSW entry point fails a filter
limitation: Release-note claims only; fixes not exercised

source_title: Read-only API key and JWTs accepted on internal gRPC API when enforce_internal_auth is enabled
claim_summary: Advisory (high, CVSS 3.1 score 8.3) states that with enforce_internal_auth enabled, read-only keys or any JWT could add a peer to the cluster and perform internal writes on port 6335; affects >=1.18.0 <1.19.2, fixed in 1.19.2; default configuration and Managed Cloud said not materially affected
limitation: No CVE ID assigned in the advisory as read on 2026-10-16; not in GitHub global advisory search or NVD keyword results; Hybrid/Private Cloud exposure depends on customer CNI per advisory; reporter credited by pseudonymous handle

claim_summary: Private Cloud 1.10.0 adds global quota enforcement (operator sets a flat 90% quota for Qdrant 1.20.0 and newer), configurable cluster domain and a TTL for retained data PVCs after cluster deletion
feature: resource quotas; data retention after deletion
limitation: References Qdrant 1.20.0, which had no GitHub release by 2026-10-16 (forward-looking); PVC retention has privacy/deletion implications not assessed

source_title: How Small Can Google's New EmbeddingGemma 2 Get?
claim_summary: With early access to Google's EmbeddingGemma 2, Qdrant reports 1-bit TurboQuant full-size vectors kept 99% of baseline nDCG@10 with 30x less vector RAM, and 256-dim 1-bit vectors with rescoring kept 94.5% at 77x less vector RAM, on five BEIR datasets
limitation: Vendor test with early model access; vector RAM excludes graph, payload and original vectors; without rescoring only ~74% of top-10 matched exact search (stated by vendor)

claim_summary: Adds Constella query encoders and the Stella document encoder, new rerankers and late-interaction models; built-in models now download from Hugging Face only (GCS fallback dropped); notes that a removed 128-token limit in several Hugging Face model configs changes embeddings of texts over 128 tokens for any fastembed version on a fresh download
limitation: Upstream model-config change alters embeddings without a library version change, a reproducibility hazard for pinned pipelines; effect size not measured
